chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام.
He was asked about tayammum, so he recited this verse:
So wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows.
"The male thief and the female thief, cut off their hands," and he said: Wipe over your two palms from the place of the cut.
And Allah, Exalted is He, said: And your Lord is never forgetful.

key_terms.أَيْدِيَكُمْ: your hands; the term examined to determine the extent of wiping
key_terms.التَّيَمُّمِ: dry ablution performed in place of wudu (ablution) or ghusl under specific circumstances
key_terms.الْمَرَافِقِ: the elbows; the limit mentioned in the verse of wudu (ablution)
key_terms.فَاغْسِلُوا: wash; an imperative command in the verse cited
key_terms.فَاقْطَعُوا: cut off; cited to clarify the Quranic usage of the word for hands
key_terms.كَفَّيْكَ: your two palms; the specific area to be wiped in tayammum here
key_terms.مَوْضِعُ الْقَطْعِ: the place of cutting; used as the marker for the extent intended
key_terms.نَسِيًّا: forgetful; negated from Allah, Exalted is He, in the cited verse

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith use Quranic verses to explain the method of tayammum?
ai.summary: This report explains the manner of tayammum through Quranic citation and inference from the wording of revealed verses. It indicates that wiping in tayammum pertains to the palms, and supports this by referencing Quranic usage and affirming that Allah, Exalted is He, is not forgetful in His expression.
